expected_behaviour: `ParsedSession::title()` returns the trimmed `session_info_name` if non-empty, else `summary::summarize_texts` over `self.messages` (src/integration/pi.rs:225-236).
how_to_test: Discover a pi session with a `session_info.name` record and confirm the picker/--list title matches it exactly; discover another with no session_info but a first user message and confirm the title is a truncated summary of that message.

feature_name: Pi Active status requires validated stable-ID + transcript-path association; absence is Unknown, never Inactive
user_story: As a Pi user, I want resume to only claim a session is Active when it has real corroborating evidence (matching session-control ID and path), never guess based on process presence alone.
expected_behaviour: `activity_status` returns `Active { observed_at }` only if `control_evidence` is `Some` and `evidence.matches(parsed)` (session_id equality plus canonicalized transcript path equality), else `Unknown` — never `Inactive` (src/integration/pi.rs:634-655,657-673).
how_to_test: Feed `activity_status` a mismatched or absent SessionControlEvidence and confirm the result is Unknown; feed a genuinely matching one and confirm Active with the evidence's observed_at.

feature_name: Pi sessions get BroadWorkspace risk when recorded cwd is $HOME or /
user_story: As a Pi user, I want a pi session recorded against my entire home directory to be flagged risky, same as other integrations.
expected_behaviour: `risk_status` (pi) delegates to `crate::scope::broad_workspace_risk` on the parsed workspace evidence (src/integration/pi.rs:756-766).
how_to_test: Craft a pi session fixture whose header cwd is exactly $HOME, run `resume --list --agent pi`, and confirm it's flagged BroadWorkspace risk on selection.

feature_name: Pi discovery filters sessions by authoritative header cwd against Scope, not directory layout
user_story: As a Pi user, I want scope filtering to be based on the actual recorded working directory in each session's header, not on the (possibly encoded) directory it's stored under.
expected_behaviour: `discover()` applies `config.scope.contains(...)` against `parsed.workspace` (the header `cwd`), incrementing `outcome.out_of_scope` and skipping when out of range; directory names under the grouped session root are never reversed to infer workspace (src/integration/pi.rs:328-372, module doc comment).
how_to_test: Place two pi session fixtures with different header cwd values under the same encoded-workspace directory (or across directories) and confirm Scope filtering follows only the header cwd values, not directory grouping.

feature_name: Claude root resolution: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR overrides default ~/.claude
user_story: As a Claude Code user with a nondefault config directory, I want resume to discover sessions from CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR when set.
expected_behaviour: `resolve_root` returns `ClaudeRoot { effective_root: PathBuf::from(explicit), nondefault: true }` when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set and non-empty, else `home.join(".claude")` with `nondefault: false` (src/integration/claude/mod.rs:100-115).
how_to_test: Set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to a custom directory with claude project fixtures and confirm `resume --list --agent claude` discovers sessions there.

feature_name: Claude identity contract: filename UUID matching embedded sessionId yields Supported
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want a session to be marked resumable only when resume can confirm its ID with high confidence (filename and embedded ID agree), never guessed.
expected_behaviour: `parse_candidate` sets `(OsString::from(embedded), SupportStatus::Supported)` only when `uuid_agrees(&filename_uuid_str, embedded)` is true (case-insensitive, brace-trimmed comparison via `normalize_uuid`) (src/integration/claude/mod.rs:396-419,536-548).
how_to_test: Create a Claude transcript `<uuid>.jsonl` whose embedded `sessionId` exactly matches the filename UUID (case-insensitively) and confirm it discovers as Supported/READY.

feature_name: Claude identity disagreement: DiscoverOnly with cwd, skipped entirely without cwd
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want resume to never silently resume under a guessed ID when the filename and embedded sessionId disagree — surfaced for visibility only if there's at least a recorded cwd.
expected_behaviour: When `uuid_agrees` is false: if `parsed.cwd.is_none()`, `parse_candidate` returns `Err(diagnostic_chain("claude_identity_disagreement", ...))` (fully skipped); otherwise it returns `SupportStatus::DiscoverOnly` (src/integration/claude/mod.rs:400-419).
how_to_test: Create a Claude transcript whose filename UUID and embedded sessionId disagree but which has a valid cwd; confirm it appears as DISCOVER, not resumable; then create one with the same disagreement but no cwd at all, and confirm it's skipped entirely (absent from --list/--json) with a claude_identity_disagreement diagnostic.

feature_name: Claude transcripts with no embedded sessionId: DiscoverOnly with cwd, skipped without
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want a transcript with no embedded sessionId at all to still be discoverable for diagnosis (if it at least has a cwd), but never treated as confidently resumable.
expected_behaviour: When `parsed.session_id` is `None`: if `parsed.cwd.is_none()`, returns `Err(diagnostic_chain("claude_no_session_id", ...))`; otherwise uses the filename stem as the id with `SupportStatus::DiscoverOnly` (src/integration/claude/mod.rs:420-433) — this exact scenario is the one referenced by the app.rs test `non_verbose_diagnostics_collapse_by_category_summing_counts`'s `claude_no_session_id` fixture (src/app.rs:963-1008).
how_to_test: Create a Claude transcript with no `sessionId` field anywhere but a valid `cwd`, confirm it shows DISCOVER status; create another with neither sessionId nor cwd, and confirm it's skipped with a claude_no_session_id diagnostic.

feature_name: Claude weak-identity diagnostic when filename isn't UUID-shaped and no sessionId exists
user_story: As a Claude Code user diagnosing discovery with --verbose, I want to know when a DiscoverOnly session's identity is especially unconfirmed (non-UUID filename, no embedded ID).
expected_behaviour: `parse_candidate` pushes a non-fatal `claude_weak_identity` diagnostic when `parsed.session_id.is_none() && !looks_like_uuid(&filename_uuid_str)` (src/integration/claude/mod.rs:453-460), using an 8-4-4-4-12 hex-group UUID shape check (`looks_like_uuid`, src/integration/claude/mod.rs:553-570).
how_to_test: Create a Claude transcript file named something non-UUID-shaped (e.g. `notes.jsonl`) with a valid cwd and no sessionId; run `resume --verbose --list --agent claude` and confirm a claude_weak_identity diagnostic appears on stderr.

feature_name: Claude title precedence: explicit agent/display name, then AI title, then human-message summary
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want the most authoritative name Claude itself assigned to show first, falling back gracefully.
expected_behaviour: `parse_candidate` computes `title = parsed.agent_name.clone().or_else(|| parsed.ai_title.clone()).or_else(|| summary::summarize_texts(...))` (src/integration/claude/mod.rs:462-473); explicitly documented as 'Resume presentation, not a claim of native picker equivalence' (module doc comment, README.md's 'Preview parsing' note).
how_to_test: Create fixtures exercising each precedence level independently (agent-name only, ai-title only, neither) and confirm the displayed title follows agent-name > ai-title > summary in each case.

feature_name: Claude Workspace comes only from event cwd, never the workspace-key directory name
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want resume to never guess my project directory from Claude's lossy, collision-prone encoded directory name.
expected_behaviour: Module doc comment states the workspace-key directory name 'is never reversed to infer Workspace'; `parse_candidate` builds `WorkspaceEvidence::Recorded { workspace: cwd, ... }` strictly from `parsed.cwd` extracted from event `cwd` fields, never from `candidate.path`'s parent directory name (src/integration/claude/mod.rs:435-441, `interpret_record`'s cwd extraction at 255-262).
how_to_test: Name a workspace-key directory something that doesn't decode back to any real path, but ensure the transcript's event cwd field is a real, valid path; confirm the discovered Workspace matches the event cwd, not anything derived from the directory name.

feature_name: Claude discovery excludes nested subagent transcripts as independent sessions
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want only top-level session transcripts shown, not internal subagent artifacts nested under a workspace-key directory.
expected_behaviour: `collect_candidates` only enumerates direct `.jsonl` children of each workspace-key directory, explicitly not descending into nested directories like `subagents/` (src/integration/claude/mod.rs:170-206, doc comment 163-168).
how_to_test: Create a workspace-key directory containing both a top-level `<uuid>.jsonl` and a `subagents/<uuid2>.jsonl`; confirm only the top-level transcript appears in discovery, never the nested subagent one.

feature_name: Claude Resume spec is exactly `claude --resume <uuid>`, never --continue
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want resume's exact resume command to match Claude's documented resume mechanism precisely, targeting the exact session rather than the ambiguous 'continue most recent' behavior.
expected_behaviour: `resume_spec` builds argv `["--resume", session.resumable_id]`, explicitly documented as 'Never `--continue`' (src/integration/claude/mod.rs:475-501, doc comment 27-30).
how_to_test: Resume a Claude session with a fake `claude` executable that echoes argv and confirm it receives exactly `--resume <uuid>`, never `--continue`.

feature_name: Claude resume preserves a nondefault CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR via environment override
user_story: As a Claude Code user with a custom config directory, I want the resumed claude process to use the same config directory resume discovered sessions from.
expected_behaviour: `resume_spec` sets `env = vec![(CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, root.effective_root)]` only when `root.nondefault` is true, else an empty env vec (src/integration/claude/mod.rs:490-497).
how_to_test: Set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to a nondefault path, resume a discovered Claude session with a fake claude binary that dumps its environment, and confirm CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is set to the same value.

feature_name: Claude resume_spec fails cleanly when there's no recorded workspace
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want resume to refuse to build a resume command for a session with no recorded cwd, rather than guessing a working directory.
expected_behaviour: `resume_spec` returns `Err(IntegrationError::InvalidSession { diagnostic: category "claude_missing_workspace" ... })` when `session.workspace.workspace()` is `None` (src/integration/claude/mod.rs:476-486).
how_to_test: Construct a Claude Session with WorkspaceEvidence::Unknown and call resume_spec directly (or via a fixture with no cwd anywhere in the transcript); confirm it errors rather than producing a spec with a fabricated cwd.

feature_name: Codex root resolution: CODEX_HOME overrides default ~/.codex
user_story: As a Codex user with a nondefault data root, I want resume to discover rollouts from CODEX_HOME when set.
expected_behaviour: `effective_root()` returns `PathBuf::from(value)` when `CODEX_HOME` is set and non-empty, else `home.join(".codex")` (src/integration/codex/mod.rs:96-102).
how_to_test: Set CODEX_HOME to a custom directory containing rollout fixtures and confirm `resume --list --agent codex` discovers sessions there.

feature_name: Codex scans both sessions/ (active) and archived_sessions/ (archived) roots
user_story: As a Codex user, I want resume to find both my current and archived sessions, distinguishing them internally without hiding archived ones by default.
expected_behaviour: `rollout_roots` includes both `<effective_root>/sessions` (RolloutKind::Active) and `<effective_root>/archived_sessions` (RolloutKind::Archived) when each exists (src/integration/codex/mod.rs:113-128); `discover_with_filter` sets `parsed.archived = root.kind == RolloutKind::Archived` for each (src/integration/codex/mod.rs:170-181).
how_to_test: Place rollout fixtures under both `sessions/` and `archived_sessions/` and confirm `resume --list --agent codex` surfaces both sets of sessions.

feature_name: Codex identity is session_meta.payload.id and Workspace is session_meta.payload.cwd, never the filename or storage directory
user_story: As a Codex user, I want resume's identity and workspace determination to be authoritative and never guessed from where the rollout file happens to live.
expected_behaviour: `parse_rollout_records` extracts `id` from `payload.get("id")` and `cwd` from `payload.get("cwd")` inside the `session_meta` record, explicitly not the unrelated `payload.session_id` nor filename nor `workspace_roots` (src/integration/codex/mod.rs:328-352, module doc comment 42-47).
how_to_test: Create a rollout file whose filename bears no relation to its session_meta.payload.id, and whose directory path differs from payload.cwd; confirm the discovered session's id/workspace match the payload fields exactly, not the filename or directory.

feature_name: Codex deduplicates user messages appearing as both event_msg and response_item
user_story: As a Codex user, I want resume's title/preview summary to not double-count the same message that Codex records twice in different record shapes.
expected_behaviour: `extract_user_messages` merges `event_msg` (`payload.type == "user_message"`) and `response_item` (`role == "user"`, `payload.type == "message"`) representations, using `push_dedup`/`fingerprint` (normalized trimmed text + attachment kind fingerprint) to avoid duplicates, capped at `MAX_USER_MESSAGES` = 1024 (src/integration/codex/mod.rs:437-462,590-611).
how_to_test: Craft a rollout with the same user text appearing once as an event_msg and once as a response_item; confirm the derived title/summary reflects it only once, not twice.

feature_name: Codex import metadata is exposed only as a coarse source-kind badge, never the origin path/remote
user_story: As a Codex user with imported sessions, I want to see that a session was imported and from what kind of source, but never have the origin's private path or git remote exposed by default.
expected_behaviour: `extract_import` reads only `foreign_session_import.source_kind` (or `kind`) into `ImportMeta { source_kind }`, explicitly never a path or remote (src/integration/codex/mod.rs:613-629, module doc comment 'Source/import badges').
how_to_test: Craft a rollout with a `foreign_session_import` payload containing both `source_kind` and a fictitious sensitive path/remote field; confirm only source_kind ever surfaces anywhere in resume's output.

feature_name: Codex Resume spec is exactly `codex -C <workspace> resume <uuid>`
user_story: As a Codex user, I want resume's exact resume command to match Codex's documented resume-by-id mechanism, explicitly not resuming by rollout path (which Codex doesn't document).
expected_behaviour: `resume_spec` builds argv `["-C", workspace, "resume", session.resumable_id]` (src/integration/codex/mod.rs:679-701), doc comment explicitly notes 'Codex 0.146.0 does not document Resume by rollout path, so the rollout path is never used as the resume locator.'
how_to_test: Resume a Codex session with a fake `codex` executable that echoes argv and confirm it receives exactly `-C <workspace> resume <uuid>`.

feature_name: Codex resume preserves CODEX_HOME based on discovery-time provenance, not a fresh env read
user_story: As a Codex user, I want resume's env override on Resume to reflect the root that actually discovered the session, even if CODEX_HOME changes between discovery and resume.
expected_behaviour: `resume_spec` derives the override from `session.key.effective_root` (captured at discovery time), not `std::env::var_os(ENV_CODEX_HOME)` freshly, only adding it when `!is_default_root(discovered_root, default_home)` (src/integration/codex/mod.rs:679-706, doc comment 'The override is derived from the session's provenance...').
how_to_test: Discover a Codex session with CODEX_HOME=/custom, then unset/change CODEX_HOME before selecting and resuming it; confirm the resumed process still receives CODEX_HOME=/custom (the discovery-time root), not the changed/absent value.

feature_name: A malformed Codex rollout file produces an isolated Error entry, never aborts discovery of other rollouts
user_story: As a Codex user, I want one corrupted rollout file to be reported and skipped, not to break discovery of all my other sessions.
expected_behaviour: `discover_with_filter` wraps each file's `parse_rollout_file` result in `DiscoveredSession::Session` or `DiscoveredSession::Error { path, error }`, continuing to the next file regardless (src/integration/codex/mod.rs:170-183); `discover_codex` in app.rs converts `Error` variants into diagnostics without stopping the loop (src/app.rs:283-303).
how_to_test: Place one intentionally-corrupt rollout JSONL alongside several valid ones under CODEX_HOME/sessions and confirm `resume --list --agent codex` still lists the valid sessions while reporting a codex diagnostic for the corrupt one.
error_notes: Ran the release binary with isolated CODEX_HOME containing two valid rollout-*.jsonl files plus rollout-corrupt.jsonl whose complete contents were the invalid JSON line `not-json`. Expected the valid sessions plus a Codex diagnostic for the corrupt file. Actual exit was 0 and valid sessions remained, but stderr was empty and JSON `errors` was []; the corrupt file was silently classified like an incomplete tail rather than reported. A valid-JSON rollout missing session_meta.payload.id did produce codex_invalid_session, but the literal corrupt-JSON scenario does not.

feature_name: Codex SQLite enrichment is compiled out by default; a plain build never links SQLite
user_story: As a user who never wants an extra native dependency, I want resume's default build to never touch state_5.sqlite at all.
expected_behaviour: `Cargo.toml`'s `[features] default = []` means `codex-sqlite` (which gates `dep:rusqlite`) is off by default (Cargo.toml `[features]` block); the non-feature `sqlite` shim module (`src/integration/codex/mod.rs` bottom, `#[cfg(not(feature = "codex-sqlite"))]`) provides a no-op `enrich()` that always returns `SqliteOutcome::Absent`.
how_to_test: Run `cargo build --locked` (default features) and confirm the resulting binary has no dynamic/static link to sqlite (e.g. via `otool -L`/`ldd`, or by confirming `rusqlite` doesn't appear in `cargo tree`).

feature_name: Codex SQLite enrichment (feature-gated) can fill missing title and activity time, never overriding JSONL identity
user_story: As a Codex user who has enabled the codex-sqlite feature, I want richer titles/activity timestamps for sessions whose rollout JSONL alone yields no usable title, sourced from Codex's own state_5.sqlite cache.
expected_behaviour: `apply_rows` (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs:409-478) only sets `session.sqlite_title` when `session.user_messages.is_empty()` and a matching row has a non-empty title, and always treats `activity_time`/`archived` as additive/enrich-only; `derive_title` in mod.rs only falls back to `sqlite_title` when the JSONL-derived summary is `None` (src/integration/codex/mod.rs 'derive_title').
how_to_test: Build with `--features codex-sqlite`, craft a rollout with no usable user messages but a matching state_5.sqlite row with a title, and confirm the picker/--list title reflects the DB title only in that fallback case, never overriding a JSONL-derivable title.

feature_name: Codex SQLite row disagreeing on id/cwd is dropped with a diagnostic, never overrides JSONL identity
user_story: As a Codex user, I want a corrupted or stale state_5.sqlite row that disagrees with the rollout's real id/cwd to be ignored for identity purposes, with a diagnostic so I can notice the inconsistency.
expected_behaviour: `apply_rows` checks `row.id` against `session.id` and `row.cwd` against `session.cwd`; on any disagreement it pushes a `codex_sqlite_id_mismatch`/`codex_sqlite_workspace_mismatch` diagnostic and `continue`s without enriching that session (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs:426-452).
how_to_test: Build with `--features codex-sqlite`, craft a state_5.sqlite row whose id or cwd disagrees with a matching rollout's session_meta, and confirm (a) the session's JSONL-derived identity/workspace are unaffected and (b) a mismatch diagnostic appears with --verbose.
error_notes: Built the release binary with --features codex-sqlite, created an isolated rollout with authoritative id DB-FALLBACK/cwd plus a matching state_5.sqlite row whose thread_id was WRONG-ID, then ran `resume <workspace> --json --verbose --agent codex`. Expected JSONL id/workspace unchanged and a codex_sqlite_id_mismatch diagnostic. Actual identity/workspace stayed correct and the DB title was rejected, but stderr was empty and JSON `errors` was []; app discovery drops SQLite enrichment diagnostics, so --verbose does not surface the required mismatch diagnostic. The internal feature test detects it, confirming the diagnostic is computed but lost at the real CLI boundary.

feature_name: Codex SQLite enrichment degrades silently (Absent) when the DB file doesn't exist
user_story: As a Codex user without a state_5.sqlite file (e.g. a fresh Codex install), I want discovery to work identically to the non-enriched path with no warning noise.
expected_behaviour: `enrich()` returns `SqliteOutcome::Absent` immediately when `!db_path.is_file()` (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs:118-121); `SqliteOutcome::summary()` returns `None` for `Absent`, so no warning is surfaced (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs:82-83).
how_to_test: Build with `--features codex-sqlite`, ensure no state_5.sqlite exists under CODEX_HOME, run `resume --list --agent codex`, and confirm output is byte-for-byte identical to the same run without the feature enabled, with no enrichment-related diagnostic.

feature_name: Codex SQLite enrichment degrades to Degraded{corrupt/locked/unsupported_schema} without blocking discovery
user_story: As a Codex user whose state_5.sqlite happens to be corrupted, locked, or has an unrecognized schema, I want Codex session discovery to keep working via JSONL, with at most a coarse warning, never a crash or blocked discovery.
expected_behaviour: `enrich()` classifies `open_readonly`/`detect_schema`/`read_rows` failures into `SqliteOutcome::Degraded { category: "locked"|"corrupt"|"unreadable"|"schema_unreadable"|"unsupported_schema"|"query_failed" }`, always falling back to unmodified JSONL-derived sessions (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs:118-166); `SqliteOutcome::summary()` renders a `codex_sqlite_degraded: <category> (falling back to JSONL)` line for Degraded outcomes (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs:88-90).
how_to_test: Build with `--features codex-sqlite`, write a garbage (non-SQLite) file at state_5.sqlite's path, run `resume --list --agent codex`, and confirm Codex sessions still discover correctly from JSONL with no crash (verify the degraded summary is at least computed, even if app.rs doesn't yet surface `SqliteOutcome::summary()` as a diagnostic — check whether app.rs's discover_codex actually surfaces this summary).

feature_name: Codex SQLite is always opened read-only via a URI with mode=ro, never immutable=1 on a live DB
user_story: As a Codex user, I want resume to never risk corrupting or interfering with Codex's own concurrently-written state_5.sqlite.
expected_behaviour: `open_readonly` builds `file:<path>?mode=ro` and opens with `SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY | SQLITE_OPEN_URI | SQLITE_OPEN_NO_MUTEX`, explicitly never `immutable=1` on a live WAL DB (documented rationale at src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs:180-198); a `assert_readonly` test helper confirms a write attempt (`CREATE TABLE`) fails on the opened connection (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs:466-473).
how_to_test: Build with `--features codex-sqlite` and run the crate's own `assert_readonly`-backed test suite (`cargo test --features codex-sqlite`), or independently open the same DB file with the same URI/flags and attempt a write, confirming it's rejected.

feature_name: OMP base config root resolution: PI_CONFIG_DIR overrides default ~/.omp
user_story: As an OMP user with a nondefault base config directory, I want resume to discover sessions relative to PI_CONFIG_DIR when set.
expected_behaviour: `config_root` returns `inputs.config_dir_env.clone()` when set, else `home.join(".omp")` (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:236-242).
how_to_test: Set PI_CONFIG_DIR to a custom directory containing omp agent fixtures and confirm `resume --list --agent omp` discovers sessions there.

feature_name: OMP profile selection precedence: --profile flag > OMP_PROFILE > PI_PROFILE
user_story: As an OMP user with multiple named profiles, I want resume to select the profile using the same precedence OMP itself uses.
expected_behaviour: `select_profile` checks `inputs.profile_flag`, then `inputs.omp_profile_env` (OMP_PROFILE), then `inputs.pi_profile_env` (PI_PROFILE), each requiring a non-whitespace-only value, defaulting to `ProfileSelection::Default` (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:204-222).
how_to_test: Set both OMP_PROFILE=work and PI_PROFILE=personal and confirm resume selects the 'work' profile's sessions; then also set --profile personal on the CLI-equivalent input and confirm it overrides both env vars.

feature_name: OMP discovery enumerates the default profile plus every named profile under profiles/
user_story: As an OMP user with several named profiles, I want `resume --list` to surface sessions from all of them at once, not just whichever one is currently selected by env vars.
expected_behaviour: `discover_omp` in app.rs starts with `base_roots` (default/env-selected profile) then reads `base_roots.config_root.join(PROFILES_DIR_NAME)` and resolves an additional `EffectiveRoots` for every named-profile subdirectory found, deduping by `profile` (src/app.rs:340-361).
how_to_test: Create session fixtures under both the default OMP profile and two named profiles (`profiles/work`, `profiles/personal`), run `resume --list --agent omp`, and confirm sessions from all three appear, each tagged with the correct profile in the agent[profile] display.

feature_name: Named OMP profiles deliberately ignore PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR and XDG_DATA_HOME overrides
user_story: As an OMP user, I want named-profile agent roots to always be `<config-root>/profiles/<name>/agent`, unaffected by env vars that only apply to the unprofiled default.
expected_behaviour: `agent_root` for `ProfileSelection::Named(name)` always returns `config_root.join(PROFILES_DIR_NAME).join(name).join(PROFILE_AGENT_DIR_NAME)`, explicitly bypassing the `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`/`XDG_DATA_HOME` branches that only apply to `ProfileSelection::Default` (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:245-268), module doc comment: 'named profiles deliberately ignore it.'
how_to_test: Set PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR to some other directory while also having a named OMP profile 'work'; confirm the 'work' profile's sessions are still discovered from `<config-root>/profiles/work/agent`, unaffected by PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR.

feature_name: OMP parses a title sidecar record that may precede the v3 session header, without assuming header position
user_story: As an OMP user, I want resume to correctly read my session's title even though OMP writes a padded title record before the actual session header, unlike Pi's header-first assumption.
expected_behaviour: `find_session_header` scans all records for `type == "session"` rather than assuming position 0 (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:711-716, module doc 'we must not reuse Pi's header-position assumptions'); `extract_session` processes `type == "title"` sidecar records via `TitleState::set` regardless of their position relative to the header (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:636-724).
how_to_test: Create an OMP session fixture with a `{type:"title", v:1, title:"my title"}` record appearing before the `{type:"session", ...}` header record, and confirm the discovered title is 'my title'.

feature_name: OMP title_change records update the effective title; the latest non-empty title wins
user_story: As an OMP user who renamed a session mid-conversation, I want the picker to show my most recent title, not the original one.
expected_behaviour: `TitleState::set` only overwrites `current` when the new title is non-empty after trim, and records are processed in file order so a later `title_change` naturally overrides an earlier title/header value (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:628-634,660-704).
how_to_test: Create an OMP fixture with an initial header title, followed by a `title_change` record with a different title; confirm the discovered/displayed title is the title_change value, not the original header title.

feature_name: OMP excludes agent/system/tool-attributed messages from the human user-message set
user_story: As an OMP user, I want resume's title/preview summary to be based only on things I actually typed, not on agent-injected or automated content mislabeled with role=user.
expected_behaviour: `is_user_attributed` inspects `attribution.source`/`source`/`meta.source` across record and message_obj, rejecting values `agent|assistant|system|tool|injected|auto|automated`, plus explicit boolean `injected`/`automated` flags (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:753-796); only messages passing this check are added to `messages` in `extract_session` (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:766-780... actual call site near 'is_user_attributed(record, message_obj)').
how_to_test: Create an OMP fixture with a `message.role="user"` record whose `attribution.source` is `"agent"`, and confirm that message never appears in the derived title/summary, unlike a genuinely user-attributed message.

feature_name: OMP import metadata is exposed only as a safe badge (source kind + short origin id prefix), never the origin path/remote in full
user_story: As an OMP user with sessions imported from Codex/Claude, I want to see that a session was imported and from where in coarse terms, without exposing the full origin session ID or path as a resumable locator.
expected_behaviour: `ImportBadge::to_display` builds `"imported from {source_kind}"` plus, if present, `"origin:<first 8 chars of origin_id>"` — never the full ID, never `origin_cwd` in the display, and the badge is explicitly documented as never merged with the origin session (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:322-338, module doc 'Imported Sessions').
how_to_test: Create an OMP fixture with a `foreign_session_import` custom entry with a long `origin_id` and `origin_cwd`; confirm any surfaced import badge shows only the source kind and an 8-character id prefix, never the full id or cwd.
error_notes: Ran isolated real binary with an OMP foreign_session_import containing origin_id 1234567890abcdef and origin_cwd /SECRET/PATH, using --list and --json. Expected a surfaced safe badge such as 'imported from codex origin:12345678' with no full ID/cwd. Actual output contained no import badge at all (only status/agent/time/title/workspace in --list and the fixed JSON schema fields). Although the internal to_display unit test safely truncates, the user-facing feature described as exposed/surfaced is missing.

feature_name: OMP default-profile Resume spec is exactly `omp --resume <id>`
user_story: As an OMP user on the default profile, I want resume's exact resume command to match OMP's own resume mechanism precisely.
expected_behaviour: `resume_spec` for `ProfileSelection::Default` (no `--profile` prefix pushed) builds argv `["--resume", id]`, adding `["--session-dir", root]` only for a custom session root (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:365-398).
how_to_test: Resume a default-profile OMP session with a fake `omp` executable that echoes argv and confirm it receives exactly `--resume <id>`.

feature_name: OMP named-profile Resume spec is exactly `omp --profile <name> --resume <id>`
user_story: As an OMP user on a named profile, I want the resume command to explicitly select that profile so I land back in the right isolated OMP context.
expected_behaviour: `resume_spec` prepends `["--profile", name]` before `["--resume", id]` when `roots.profile` is `ProfileSelection::Named(name)` (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:365-380).
how_to_test: Resume a named-profile ('work') OMP session with a fake `omp` executable and confirm argv is exactly `--profile work --resume <id>`.

feature_name: OMP resume always propagates PI_CONFIG_DIR to the discovered config root
user_story: As an OMP user, I want the resumed omp process to resolve the same base config/profile that discovery used, even for the default profile.
expected_behaviour: `resume_env` unconditionally returns `vec![(PI_CONFIG_DIR, roots.config_root)]` regardless of profile or whether the root is nondefault (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:401-414), unlike Claude/Codex which only propagate when nondefault — a documented asymmetry worth noting between integrations.
how_to_test: Resume both a default-profile and a named-profile OMP session with a fake omp binary dumping env, and confirm PI_CONFIG_DIR is always set to the discovered config root in both cases, even when it equals the default ~/.omp.

feature_name: OMP Active status requires live process + TTY + matching terminal breadcrumb all agreeing; a stale breadcrumb alone is Unknown
user_story: As an OMP user, I want resume to only claim Active when it has strong, multi-signal evidence (not just a leftover breadcrumb file from a closed terminal).
expected_behaviour: `ActivityEvidence::matches` requires `live_process`, `tty.is_some()`, and `breadcrumb_alive` to all be true, plus the breadcrumb's session path canonicalizing to the same file as the parsed transcript, before returning true (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:940-953); `activity_status` maps anything else to `Unknown` (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:909-920).
how_to_test: Feed `activity_status` an `ActivityEvidence` with `breadcrumb_alive: false` (or `live_process: false`) and confirm the result is Unknown, not Active; then feed one with all three conditions true and matching paths, confirming Active.

feature_name: OMP discovery filters sessions by authoritative header cwd against Scope, never directory layout
user_story: As an OMP user, I want scope filtering based on the real recorded working directory in each session, consistent with the other integrations.
expected_behaviour: `discover()` (omp) applies `config.scope.contains(...)` against `parsed.workspace` from the header `cwd`, incrementing `outcome.out_of_scope` when excluded (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:958-1000), mirroring pi's approach.
how_to_test: Place OMP session fixtures with different header cwd values and confirm Scope filtering (e.g. --up/--down) follows only the header cwd, not the storage directory structure.

feature_name: resume never performs a machine-wide scan; only known integration roots + Scope filtering
user_story: As a user, I want assurance that resume only looks at the specific, documented session-storage locations for enabled agents, never crawling arbitrary parts of my filesystem.
expected_behaviour: Each integration's discovery starts from a resolved, documented root (`~/.pi/agent`, `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.omp` or their env overrides) and only recurses within that root's `.jsonl` files (e.g. `collect_jsonl` in pi.rs/omp/mod.rs, `list_rollout_files_into` in codex/mod.rs, `collect_candidates` in claude/mod.rs); README.md states this explicitly ('It does not recursively search the machine...').
how_to_test: Run `resume --verbose --list` under `strace`/`dtruss`/`fs_usage` (platform-appropriate) and confirm all directory reads are confined to the resolved agent roots and their subdirectories, never an unrelated filesystem-wide walk.

feature_name: Discovery and Preview never modify session files, mtimes, or directory entries
user_story: As a user, I want resume's read-only discovery/preview to never risk corrupting or altering my agent's session history.
expected_behaviour: All discovery reads go through `jsonl::read_file_confined`/`open_for_read`, which opens files for read only (`fs::File::open`, never `OpenOptions::write`); `src/snapshot.rs`'s `DirSnapshot` helpers exist specifically to regression-test byte/mtime/entry immutability before and after discovery in the integration test suites.
how_to_test: Snapshot a fixture agent root's file bytes/mtimes/directory entries (e.g. via `snapshot_dir`), run `resume --list`/`resume --json` against it, re-snapshot, and confirm the two snapshots are identical.

feature_name: Session-file symlinks are confined to the effective configured root; cross-boundary symlinks are rejected
user_story: As a user, I want a maliciously or accidentally planted symlink inside an agent's session directory pointing outside that root to never be silently followed and surfaced as a 'resumable session'.
expected_behaviour: `jsonl::open_for_read` canonicalizes the target path and rejects it via `io::Error::other(...)` when `!resolved.starts_with(root)` (src/jsonl.rs:94-113); all four integrations now route production reads through `read_file_confined` with their real effective root, per docs/review/round-2-sonnet-verification.md's verification of the round-1 finding #1 fix (originally flagged in docs/review/round-1-sonnet.md finding #1).
how_to_test: Create a symlink inside e.g. CODEX_HOME/sessions pointing to a file outside CODEX_HOME (a different tempdir), run `resume --list --agent codex`, and confirm the symlinked file's content never surfaces as a session, with a diagnostic reflecting the rejection.
error_notes: Created CODEX_HOME/sessions/2026/1/1/evil.jsonl as a symlink to an outside tempdir transcript containing session id EVIL, then ran the isolated real binary with --verbose --json --agent codex. The outside content was correctly not surfaced, but stdout was {schemaVersion:1,sessions:[],errors:[]} and stderr was empty. Expected both rejection and a diagnostic reflecting it; the diagnostic is missing from the real CLI path.

feature_name: Attachments are represented by safe placeholders, never raw base64/pixel/file data
user_story: As a user, I want images/files referenced in my sessions to never have their raw bytes echoed into the picker preview, list output, or JSON.
expected_behaviour: `Attachment::Image`/`Attachment::File` variants carry only `media_type`/`filename` metadata and a static placeholder note (`[image]`/`[file]`), never a data field; `Attachment::to_display` never emits base64, regression-tested by `image_attachment_uses_placeholder_not_base64` and `extract_array_with_text_and_image_blocks`'s comment 'The base64 data is never stored in the attachment' (src/message.rs:139-147, 189-203).
how_to_test: Craft a session fixture with an image attachment carrying a large base64 `data` field, and confirm neither `--json` nor the preview pane ever contains that base64 string.

feature_name: Injection filtering collapses only known, complete wrapper tags, never arbitrary user XML/HTML
user_story: As a user, I want my own genuine code or markup containing XML/HTML-like tags to survive display unmangled, while known agent-injected wrappers (like <skill>) are stripped.
expected_behaviour: `collapse_known_injections` only touches tags in `KNOWN_WRAPPERS` (`["skill"]`) and only when fully matched (open+close present); unknown tags, attributed tags (`<skill id="x">`), and incomplete pairs are left untouched (src/injection.rs:1-33, tests at lines 70+ e.g. `preserves_genuine_xml_tags`, `preserves_unknown_xml_wrappers`, `does_not_match_tag_with_attributes`).
how_to_test: Feed a message containing `<root><child>value</child></root>` alongside a genuine `<skill>injected</skill>` wrapper and confirm only the skill wrapper collapses while the root/child XML is preserved verbatim in the displayed title/preview.

feature_name: All rendered text (rows, preview, titles) is stripped of ANSI/CSI/OSC/C1/bidi control sequences
user_story: As a user, I want a session containing malicious ANSI escape sequences (e.g. a fake OSC 8 hyperlink, terminal title hijack, or bidi-override filename spoofing) in its content to never be able to manipulate my terminal when displayed.
expected_behaviour: `text::strip_terminal_controls`/`text::normalize` remove ESC-led CSI/OSC/DCS/SOS/PM/APC sequences, C0/C1 controls, DEL, and bidi/invisible Unicode controls while preserving ordinary Unicode; the picker's `sanitize_for_display` applies the equivalent stripping before any `AnsiString`/`ItemPreview::Text` construction (src/text.rs full module; src/picker.rs `sanitize_for_display`); adversarial test `no_output_can_contain_escape_byte` asserts across many attack strings and both Normalized/Raw modes that no ESC or BEL byte ever survives (src/text.rs 'no_output_can_contain_escape_byte' test).
how_to_test: Craft a session title containing an OSC 8 hyperlink payload, a terminal-title-set OSC 0 sequence, and a bidi-override character; run `resume --list`/open the picker preview and confirm none of these sequences execute or alter the terminal (e.g. capture raw stdout bytes and grep for ESC 0x1b).

feature_name: Preview cache is process-only in-memory (bounded LRU), with no persistent disk cache
user_story: As a user, I want no on-disk cache file that could leak session preview content to other users or processes on the same machine after resume exits.
expected_behaviour: `PreviewCache` is a `Mutex`-guarded in-memory `HashMap` bounded to 64 MiB total / 16 MiB per item with LRU eviction, with no file-backed persistence anywhere in `src/preview.rs`; README.md states 'There is no persistent Preview cache and no machine-wide scan.'
how_to_test: Run resume interactively, open several previews, exit, and confirm (e.g. via `lsof`/filesystem search) no cache file was written anywhere on disk for preview content.

feature_name: DOC/CODE MISMATCH: README's row format table implies a live BRANCH column, but the code hardcodes '-'
user_story: As a QA reader relying on the README's picker row description, I want to know that the documented 'BRANCH' column position never actually contains a git branch name in v0.1.0, so expectations are set correctly.
expected_behaviour: README.md's 'Picker row format' text and the picker_candidate implementation both name a branch position, but `picker_candidate` literally sets `let branch = "-";` with no code path ever populating it from git (src/app.rs:471); this is not called out as a known limitation anywhere in README.md or CONTEXT.md.
how_to_test: Compare README.md's row-format description against `resume --list` output on a session inside a non-default git branch and confirm the branch field is always '-', flag for docs update or feature completion in a later phase.
error_notes: README's picker/list row-format section now states that BRANCH is always literal '-' in v0.1.0 and is a placeholder for a future feature, not live Git-branch data.

feature_name: DOC/CODE MISMATCH: README states 'A Git failure is reported as a diagnostic', but build_scope's git_warning string is not wired into DiscoveryState.errors
user_story: As a QA reader, I want to verify README's claim that a Git Scope discovery failure surfaces as a diagnostic, since the current code path constructs the warning string but does not appear to feed it into the same DiagnosticCollector/DiscoveryState.errors path other diagnostics use.
expected_behaviour: `build_scope` constructs `DefaultScope::Exact { git_warning: Some(error.to_string()) }` (src/app.rs:130-140) but this `git_warning` field is never read anywhere else in app.rs (no `state.errors.lock().unwrap().push(...)` call references it) — the warning appears to be silently discarded rather than surfacing on stderr as README.md's 'A Git failure is reported as a diagnostic' claims.
how_to_test: Force `discover_git_scope` to fail (e.g. break the git binary or run in a corrupted .git directory) and run `resume --verbose --list`; confirm whether any diagnostic line about the git failure actually appears on stderr, or whether the README claim is currently inaccurate.
error_notes: Ran release `resume --verbose --list` in an isolated HOME with a fake git executable that printed `secret-git-failure` and exited 1. Expected README-promised Git failure diagnostic; actual exit was 0 with empty stderr. The git_warning produced by build_scope is silently discarded.

feature_name: DOC/CODE MISMATCH: CONTEXT.md defines four Support Status values (Supported/Discover Only/Unsupported/Unavailable), but Unsupported is never assigned by any integration
user_story: As a QA reader, I want to confirm whether 'Unsupported' is a live, reachable status in v0.1.0 or purely a modeled-but-unused enum variant, since CONTEXT.md's Support Status definition implies all four are meaningfully distinguishable today.
expected_behaviour: CONTEXT.md defines Support Status as one of 'Supported, Discover Only, Unsupported, or Unavailable'; grep across src/integration/*/mod.rs shows only `SupportStatus::Supported`, `SupportStatus::DiscoverOnly`, and (via app.rs's `normalize_availability`) `SupportStatus::Unavailable` are ever constructed — `SupportStatus::Unsupported` has no production call site in v0.1.0's four integrations.
how_to_test: Grep `SupportStatus::Unsupported` across src/ and confirm zero non-enum-definition, non-launch.rs-display production assignment sites exist; note this as a gap between CONTEXT.md's stated four-way status model and actual v0.1.0 behavior.
error_notes: CONTEXT.md now states that only Supported, Discover Only, and Unavailable are reachable in v0.1.0; Unsupported is modeled for a future integration and is not currently assigned.

feature_name: DOC/CODE MISMATCH: RiskStatus::WorkspaceChanged and ConflictingMetadata are modeled and drive prompt text, but no discovery path ever assigns them
user_story: As a QA reader, I want to confirm which of the four RiskStatus variants are actually reachable via normal discovery, since the confirmation-prompt code (launch::risk_reasons) implies all four are live signals.
expected_behaviour: `RiskStatus` has `Normal, BroadWorkspace, WorkspaceChanged, ConflictingMetadata` (src/session.rs:49-55); `risk_reasons` handles all four (src/launch.rs:142-156); but only `Normal` and `BroadWorkspace` are ever produced by any of the four integrations' discovery code — `WorkspaceChanged`/`ConflictingMetadata` risk (as opposed to the separately-implemented revalidate-time WorkspaceChanged error) are dead states in v0.1.0, per docs/review/round-1-sonnet.md finding #3 ('NITPICK').
how_to_test: Grep `RiskStatus::WorkspaceChanged` and `RiskStatus::ConflictingMetadata` production assignment sites across src/integration/*/mod.rs and confirm none exist outside test code; note as a documentation/behavior gap for future phases.
error_notes: CONTEXT.md now documents WorkspaceChanged and ConflictingMetadata as reserved, currently unproduced discovery variants and distinguishes the separate launch-revalidation WorkspaceChanged error.

feature_name: DOC/CODE MISMATCH RISK: cli::config_example()'s literal string is not automatically kept in sync with Config's schema by a compile-time or test-time check
user_story: As a QA reader, I want to confirm whether `resume config example`'s output is guaranteed (by a test) to always be loadable by `resume --config`, so a future field rename can't silently desynchronize documentation from the real schema.
expected_behaviour: `config_example()` returns a hand-written `&'static str` literal (src/cli.rs:99-105) with no test in src/cli.rs or src/config.rs that parses this literal through `config::load_path`/`toml::from_str::<Config>` to confirm it stays valid as the schema evolves.
how_to_test: Search src/cli.rs and src/config.rs test modules for any test asserting `toml::from_str::<Config>(config_example())` succeeds; if none exists, flag this as a regression risk for later phases (a future field addition/removal to `Config` could silently break the documented example without any test failing).
error_notes: Added config_example_round_trips_through_config_schema, which parses config_example() as Config and asserts every documented field value; schema/example drift now fails the test suite.

feature_name: DOC/CODE MISMATCH: README's 'Isolation preserved when applicable' column implies OMP's env propagation is conditional like Claude/Codex, but OMP always propagates PI_CONFIG_DIR
user_story: As a QA reader comparing the README's Native Resume boundary table to the actual per-agent env logic, I want to know that OMP's propagation is unconditional while Claude/Codex only propagate on a nondefault root, since the README phrasing ('nondefault CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR' / 'nondefault CODEX_HOME' vs 'config/root environment') could read as parallel but the implementations differ.
expected_behaviour: Claude's `resume_spec` only adds `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when `root.nondefault` (src/integration/claude/mod.rs:490-497); Codex's `resume_spec` only adds `CODEX_HOME` when `!is_default_root(...)` (src/integration/codex/mod.rs:696-701); OMP's `resume_env` always includes `PI_CONFIG_DIR` regardless of whether it's the default `~/.omp` (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:401-414) — a real behavioral asymmetry not explicitly called out in README.md's Native Resume boundary table.
how_to_test: Resume a default-profile OMP session where PI_CONFIG_DIR was never set (using the plain ~/.omp default) with a fake omp binary dumping env, and confirm PI_CONFIG_DIR is present in its environment even though it's the default location — contrasted with a default-CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR Claude resume, which gets no CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR override at all.
error_notes: Inspected and exercised isolated fake-agent launch setup; literal interactive launch could not be completed because the harness lacked a controlling TTY, so verified the equivalent ResumeSpec mechanism. OMP resume_env unconditionally emits PI_CONFIG_DIR, while Claude/Codex conditionally emit root overrides. The README does not disclose this confirmed asymmetry.

feature_name: --since <YYYY-MM-DD> filters Sessions by an absolute cutoff date
user_story: As a user, I want to filter Sessions to those active on or after a specific calendar date, so I can find work from a known point in time without computing a relative duration.
expected_behaviour: `Since::from_str` recognizes a strict `YYYY-MM-DD` shape and parses it as UTC midnight via `crate::time::parse_iso8601` (src/cli.rs); resolves to a fixed cutoff `SystemTime` regardless of `now` (`Since::cutoff` returns the date verbatim for the `Date` variant).
how_to_test: Run `resume --json --since 2020-01-01` against real session data and confirm sessions older than that date are excluded; run `resume --since 2026-13-40` (invalid date) and confirm exit code 2.

feature_name: --since all explicitly disables time filtering (also the default)
user_story: As a user who has set a default since cutoff in config, I want `--since all` on the command line to show every Session regardless of activity age, overriding the config default for this one invocation.
expected_behaviour: `Since::All` resolves to `cutoff() -> None`, and `effective_options` treats a `None` cutoff as no filtering at all in `session_at_or_after` (src/app.rs); this is also the behavior when `--since` and config `since` are both absent.
how_to_test: Run `resume --json --since all` and confirm it returns the same session set as omitting `--since` entirely; covered by `since_all_matches_since_flag_absent` in tests/step9_app.rs.

feature_name: --since compares against transcript file mtime when no richer activity signal is available
user_story: As a user, I want --since to work consistently across all four agents even though only some of them expose a rich activity timestamp, so the flag is never silently a no-op for a given agent.
expected_behaviour: `session_at_or_after` (src/app.rs) resolves each Session's transcript path via `record_transcript_path` (direct for Pi/Claude/OMP native_locator, via the `native_id::path` split for Codex) and stats the file's own mtime as the filter signal; a Session whose transcript cannot be stat'd is conservatively kept rather than hidden, since Discovery already surfaces unavailable Sessions for diagnosis elsewhere rather than dropping them silently.
how_to_test: Backdate a fixture transcript's file mtime, confirm `--since <short-window>` excludes it; delete/rename the transcript out from under an already-discovered candidate mid-run (race scenario) and confirm the Session is still listed rather than silently vanishing.
